_readme: Real captures, and what they actually say. Used by `npm run bench-ocr`, which is a
measurement tool rather than a pass/fail test -- OCR accuracy is a number to improve, not a
thing to assert.
To add one: snip the panel with the extension, right-click the capture in the result window,
'Save image as...', and drop it here under the name below. Then fill in `text`. A fixture
with no image is skipped; so is one with no `text` recorded yet.
`text` is the reading order a human would use: for vertical text that is the rightmost
column top-to-bottom, then the next column to its left. Punctuation width does not matter --
comparison is NFKC-folded, so ! and ！ are the same character as far as the score goes.
`script` and `orientation` must match the image: they pick the starting model, and the other
sweeps run against it. They are not themselves under test -- both settings were shown to work
(chi_sim_vert scored 0.30 where every other model scored 0.70 to 1.00) and both are chosen by
the user rather than guessed.
Keep them real. A synthetic render scored 0/5 on an engine that reads clean text perfectly,
so it measured the fixture rather than the recogniser. Generating an image is out; applying a
known degradation to a real one is not, which is how the tilt sweep works.
WHAT WAS IN QUESTION: stylised lettering versus tilt, confounded in the one panel that is
both. The per-glyph sweep settled it without a second fixture -- see that fixture's note --
so what is left here is a control, not an experiment.
SETTLED FOR HAND-LETTERED SOUND EFFECTS, which are out of scope: thresholding, declared
resolution, page-segmentation mode, deskewing and the larger Tesseract models were all
measured against them and none helped. tessdata_best cannot run at all -- no tesseract.js
WASM core has the float dot-product intrinsic its weights need.
TWO THINGS DID HELP, and both ship. Enlarging, but only small captures and only by exactly
2x -- a flat multiplier ruins a large capture and a fractional one smears glyph edges. And
splitting vertical text into its columns, which took a capture Tesseract merged into
nonsense from cer 0.50 to 0.00. Both are tuned to the fixtures here and both have a
threshold guessed at inside a gap in the measurements; the SHIPPED row of the bench runs the
real rules, so re-run it after touching either.
PP-OCR was spiked against the fixture below rather than argued about: cer 0.20 against 0.30,
so better but not a fix, and it costs owning a detection-postprocessing pipeline. Cloud OCR
does read these panels (that is what Copyfish uses -- it uploads to ocr.space), and was
declined on purpose: this extension stays offline. Ordinary typeset dialogue, which is the
common case, already works.
The one idea here worth keeping if any of this is ever revisited: precision matters more than
recall. A wrong character sends the reader to a confidently wrong dictionary entry, while a
missing one costs them another snip. So an engine with trustworthy confidence, gated to drop
its own bad reads, beats a more accurate one that cannot tell when it is wrong -- and CER,
which scores both failures alike, is the wrong metric for judging that.

vertical-handletter-two-column.note: STYLISED + TILTED. The case that prompted all of this. Best so far: cer 0.30 at 2x. SETTLED by the per-glyph sweep: the glyphs that can be read at all need six different angles (+2, +4, +6, +8, 0, -2), so the tilt is per-glyph jitter and no whole-image deskew can reach it -- and four of ten stay wrong even with their own tilt corrected, so the lettering is out of distribution as well. Both causes are real, and correcting the tilt half needs per-glyph detection, which is a text detector. SCRIPT CORRECTED to traditional (was mislabelled simplified, inherited from the extension). No score moves: 啊 and 噫 are identical in both scripts, so nothing in this capture discriminates. It is fixed anyway because PP-OCRv5 selects a different recognition model per script, so the label would quietly mislead any sweep that used it -- PP-OCRv6, which ships one multi-script model, is simply indifferent.

light-on-dark-banner.note: LIGHT TEXT ON A DARK, TEXTURED BACKGROUND. Reads nothing at all rather than reading it wrong, which is the signature of inverted polarity: Tesseract expects dark on light, and its layout analysis finds no text regions to hand the recogniser. Unlike the stylised-lettering case this should be fixable in preprocessing -- see the polarity sweep. Note the script: 囉 is traditional (simplified is 啰), while the other four characters are the same either way.

horizontal-printed-clean.text: 萝萝娜的工房-我的宝物
horizontal-printed-clean.note: CONTROL. Ordinary typeset horizontal text -- the common case. Transcribed by eye; correct it if wrong.

vertical-printed-clean.note: CONTROL. Ordinary typeset vertical text, two columns -- the common case for manhua dialogue. Transcribed by eye; correct it if wrong.

traditional-vertical-two-column.text: 倖存的居民皆已收容完畢！
traditional-vertical-two-column.note: THE CAPTURE THAT PROVED COLUMN SPLITTING WAS NEEDED. Clean black on white, no tilt, typeset -- textbook conditions -- and Tesseract still merged the two columns and returned "全半已收容完畢!" for twelve characters. Reads exactly now (cer 0.00) because the columns are split before recognition. Its neighbour on the same page, traditional-vertical-three-column, needed no such help, which is what showed the fault was layout analysis rather than anything about the material.

traditional-vertical-three-column.text: 不過，船上的貨物還有一半無法回收…
traditional-vertical-three-column.note: THE CONTROL FOR COLUMN SPLITTING. The next bubble on the same page as the two-column fixture, at identical quality and scale -- and this one Tesseract already reads correctly on its own. That makes it the case column splitting could break: the code now takes apart a capture that was working. If splitting ever regresses anything, expect it here first.

noisy-background-bubble.note: KNOWN LIMITATION, MEASURED AND ACCEPTED. Text in a bubble over busy line art. The trailing ellipsis is in the image but deliberately not in `text`, because NFKC expands it into three periods and one piece of decoration then counts as three errors. The fault is OVER-detection, the opposite of the light-on-dark banner: Tesseract finds text by connected components and has no learned detector, so foliage and hatching supply endless stroke-shaped candidates. The characters themselves are legible -- at 10% inset it reads 根本 correctly, just buried in junk -- so nothing here is a recognition failure. REJECTED, with evidence: filtering words by confidence. It separates junk from signal here (0 and 7) and on the two-column fixture (0, 0, 23 for the wrong characters against 93, 84, 81 for the right ones), but horizontal-printed-clean reads 萝 twice at confidence 0 and is CORRECT -- so any threshold that removes junk deletes good text from a capture that currently scores 0.00. A low-confidence warning was considered and declined instead: the capture and the reading sit side by side in the window, so the user can already see nonsense for what it is. ALSO A COUNTEREXAMPLE to recogniserScale: 15k pixels, so it gets doubled, and doubling makes it worse (empty, against 箭本 at 1x). Not retuned, because lowering the boundary would break the hand-lettered fixture, which needs doubling at 26k. Size is not the only variable -- noise amplifies too.

_readme_game: GAME FIXTURES, added for the desktop app. Everything above came from manhua and was curated
against Tesseract's failures, which makes it a biased sample twice over: the material is one
genre, and the cases were chosen because one particular engine failed them. These are neither.
They are ordinary Genshin Impact UI, captured the way the app will actually be used, and no
engine has seen them before -- so they are the first honest test of whether PP-OCRv6's 0.000
There is no `tesseract` baseline for any of them and there never will be; the extension cannot
read a game window at all. The number to watch is simply the absolute CER.
Transcribed by eye from the images by Claude, then CHECKED BY THE CAPTURER on 2026-08-17 and
confirmed correct. That check is what makes the 0.000 mean anything: the engine agreeing with
a transcription proves nothing if the same reader produced both. Correct them if you find an
error anyway -- a mistake here is measured as an engine error forever after.
DECORATION IS EXCLUDED FROM `text`, following the precedent set by noisy-background-bubble:
the ✦ bullet in game-text-over-scene is a glyph the font draws, not language, and NFKC has no
opinion about it, so counting it would penalise a correct reading. The ellipsis in
game-tiny-text is kept because it is real punctuation in the string -- but note it costs three
errors, not one, since NFKC expands … into three periods.

game-dialogue-panel.text: 派蒙阿贝多，计划还顺利吗？
game-dialogue-panel.note: THE COMMON CASE FOR GAMES. Speaker name above, dialogue below, over a semi-translucent panel with the 3D scene showing through. Two text runs at different sizes and colours (the name is gold), so it also tests that reading order goes name-then-line rather than interleaving them.

game-dialogue-panel-2.text: 阿贝多很久以前，她将我送到蒙德，告诉我，我必须完成一个非常重大的课题：寻找世界的真相。
game-dialogue-panel-2.note: THE SAME PANEL OVER A DIFFERENT BACKGROUND, and much wider (1612px, one long line). Paired with game-dialogue-panel deliberately: the panel is translucent, so what sits behind it changes the local contrast under the glyphs. Two samples separate 'reads game dialogue' from 'reads game dialogue over this one background'. Also carries a fullwidth colon.

game-ui-small-label.note: SMALL UI CHROME, AND TWO SEPARATE LABELS. Menu buttons with a large icon above each caption. The icons are the test: they are exactly the sort of high-contrast non-text shape that made Tesseract invent characters on noisy-background-bubble, and a learned detector should ignore them. Reading order is left to right across two disconnected blocks.

game-tiny-text.note: THE SMALLEST LEGIBLE TEXT. 278x39 for nine characters, which is about 26px per glyph -- the floor for this UI. The ellipsis is real and kept, but it is worth three errors under NFKC, so a 0.25 here with everything else correct means the ellipsis alone.

game-text-over-scene.text: 获取概率提升！每十次祈愿必出四星或以上物品。活动限定五星角色仅可在UP期间，通过对应祈愿获得。具体内容查看【详情】。
game-text-over-scene.note: THREE BLOCKS, MIXED SCRIPTS, NO PANEL. A heading, a highlighted banner line in reversed colours (white on blue), and a body paragraph, all over a light gradient. Tests several things at once: multi-block reading order, latin embedded mid-sentence (UP), lenticular brackets 【】, and one run of light-on-dark inside an otherwise dark-on-light capture -- which is the light-on-dark-banner failure appearing as part of a larger image rather than on its own. The ✦ bullet is decoration and deliberately not in `text`.

game-item-description.text: 迅速投出雷楔，以疾雷之势歼敌。雷楔命中时会对小范围内的敌人造成雷元素伤害，并在命中的位置留下雷楔标记。长按长按以调整雷楔标记投掷的方向。通过长按投出的雷楔，可以悬浮在空中，并使刻晴再次施放星斗归位时跨越地形。雷楔在雷楔的持续期间内，刻晴再次施放星斗归位或施展重击时，会清除雷楔标记并造成不同的效果：·再次施放星斗归位时，瞬移到标记处进行一次斩击，造成雷元素范围伤害。瞬移至长按投掷的雷楔处时，可以跨越地形障碍；
game-item-description.note: THE LONG ONE, and the only fixture where length itself is the variable -- roughly 190 characters across many wrapped lines, against a dozen or so everywhere else. A dropped line costs far more here than a dropped glyph does anywhere else, so this is what catches a detector that loses whole rows. Also has coloured inline runs (雷元素伤害 in purple), two section headings, a lone fullwidth colon on its own line, and a middot bullet. The capture is clipped at the bottom mid-sentence, which is realistic and left as-is; `text` stops where the image does. MEASURED FAILURE: the lone ： on its own line is the one character PP-OCRv6 drops across all fourteen fixtures -- a single glyph with no line-mates, which the detector does not raise a box for.

scene-full-frame.text: 自动奈芙尔你们说得没错，我确实从你们关注的事里嗅到了蹊跷的味道，不过也就一点点。
scene-full-frame.note: A WHOLE SCREEN, NOT A SNIP. Every other fixture is a region the user framed; this is 2560x1393 of unframed game, and it exists to test DETECTION rather than recognition -- can the engine find the text among characters, furniture, plants, a lantern and a floor of flagstones? Measured: exactly three boxes, all of them real (the 自动 button, the speaker name, the line), and nothing invented. The three icon-only buttons beside 自动 are correctly ignored, having no text. That is the direct counterpart to noisy-background-bubble, where Tesseract's connected-component search turned line art into a dozen invented characters. CER is scored here but is the lesser half of the point; a regression would more likely show up as extra boxes than as wrong ones. Reading order is plain row-major top-to-bottom, which happens to be right here and would not be for a screen with side-by-side panels. Also the slowest fixture by far at ~1.8s, because nothing has cropped it -- which is the argument for the pinned-live-region mode cropping to its rectangle before reading rather than re-reading the screen.
scene-full-frame.bottom_cropped: UID removed by the capturer, so the frame is slightly shorter than the display

vertical-text-with-horizontal-number.text: 對了，現在最新的顯示卡是298喔～
vertical-text-with-horizontal-number.note: Vertical Chinese with an upright horizontal number. Detection finds both columns but recognition drops the left column. Reflowing ink bands recovers it and keeps 298 together. Known remaining error: the trailing wave dash is omitted.
